summary: Nora tidies her own notebook: notes about the same occasion are merged, and questions that have been answered or overtaken are retired.
details: Two notes about the same date AND the same people are combined into one that keeps everything both said, including any disagreement — the surviving note is the older, and the other is retired pointing at it.
A note whose occasion has passed, where the body shows the question was answered or can no longer be answered, stops appearing.
limitations: MERGING CANNOT HAPPEN YET. A note is matched by its anchor — the date AND the people it is about — and the people half is not populated anywhere in the system, so every candidate pair collides on the date alone and is refused rather than merged. Two notes about the same day but different things would otherwise be combined and neither could be recovered. The refusals are counted, so the number says what filling in the people half would unlock.
Off by default and behind three separate switches; nothing is merged or retired until an operator turns the background pass on for a room.
Nothing is deleted — a retired note stays readable, it just stops appearing in what Nora is shown.
